solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fish in various parts of Wales I have caught

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the next piece inside them, as if catching it
the parts of the word Wales are set out in a different arrangement

parts.note: I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: An angler boasts of a catch made at several spots around Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Alewives are herring-like North American fish of the shad family.

clue.text: Feature of rugby story, nothing to listen to

indicators.note: the pieces are to be heard rather than read, so their sound gives the entry

parts.note: a story can be a lie, a fib; nowt is Northern English dialect for nothing

explanation.surface: A rugby tale with nothing in it worth hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'lie nowt' runs together as the rugby term. NOWT is Northern English for nothing. A lineout is the rugby restart where forwards jump for a ball thrown in from touch.
explanation.definitionFit: The lineout is a set piece peculiar to rugby, restarting play after the ball goes into touch.

clue.text: Lawman and wife joining riotous tea party

indicators.note: wild and disorderly, so the letters of tea party are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A sheriff and his wife join a rowdy tea party.
explanation.definitionFit: Wyatt Earp was the famous Wild West marshal of the Tombstone gunfight, a byword for frontier law enforcement.

clue.text: Aperture to recover in the belly

parts.note: a vent is an opening or aperture
to rally is to recover, as a patient or a market does

explanation.surface: A hole in the stomach that helps someone get better.
explanation.definitionFit: Ventral refers to the underside or abdomen, so the adverb means on or towards the belly side.

clue.text: Getting rid of coarse cloth

definitions.meaning: rough woven material such as hessian used for sacks

explanation.surface: Throwing out some rough fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacking is both dismissal from a job and the burlap fabric sacks are made from.

clue.text: Most delightful English street shut off at the front

indicators.note: this piece goes before the others in the entry though it comes last in the clue

parts.note: to cut a supply is to shut it off

explanation.surface: A charming English street is closed at its end nearest the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute means charming or appealing, so its superlative is the most delightful.

clue.text: Deal with particular player on cricket field

parts.note: to cover a topic or task is to deal with it
a particular is a detail or point

explanation.surface: Handling one specific player during a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, cover point is a fielding position on the off side between cover and point, and also names the fielder stationed there.
explanation.definitionFit: Cover point is a fielding position, and by extension the fielder placed in it.

clue.text: Presenting restaurant's latest terrible dinner — no good

indicators.note: the latest part of the word restaurant's is its final letter
something terrible is a mess, so the fodder's letters are scrambled

parts.note: as printed the word cannot work; the setter needed denier here, a unit of yarn weight, whose letters fit exactly

explanation.surface: A dreadful meal at a restaurant is being served, and it is no good.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of DINNER cannot work: it gives one N too many and one E too few. With DENIER the anagram signalled by 'terrible' gives ENDERI, and T, ENDERI, N, G build the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tendering an offer or resignation means formally presenting or offering it.

clue.text: Sort of valley celebrated at first for wine

indicators.note: this piece comes at the front of the entry though printed later

parts.note: to have sung of something is to celebrate it in song
a ria is a long narrow inlet formed by a drowned river valley

explanation.surface: A valley once famed for its wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Sangria is a Spanish punch of red wine with fruit and lemonade.

clue.text: Occupying vessel, we hear, to no avail

indicators.note: the words are heard rather than read, so a similar-sounding phrase is entered

parts.note: a blood vessel is a vein, so being inside one is in vein

explanation.surface: Taking over a ship turns out, so we are told, to be pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, but here it is a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something to no purpose or without success is doing it fruitlessly.

clue.text: Agreement old archdeacon couched in jargon

indicators.note: expressed in, so the next pieces sit inside the jargon word

parts.note: cant is the special jargon of a group
an archdeacon is styled the Venerable, abbreviated Ven

explanation.surface: A deal made by an old churchman is phrased in impenetrable jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: A covenant is a formal binding agreement or contract.

clue.text: Female rioter in trouble with Rex, special sort of dog

indicators.note: letters in a state of upset are put into disorder

explanation.surface: A female rioter is in trouble along with someone called Rex, a common dog name.
explanation.definitionFit: The fox terrier is a breed of small terrier originally used to bolt foxes.

clue.text: See 3
Sarah collects rubbish getting about bit of America

indicators.note: the first name gathers the next piece inside it

parts.note: Sal is a pet form of Sarah
tat is shoddy goods, rubbish

explanation.surface: Sarah picks up litter as she travels around part of the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting about' looks like travel, but 'about' opens the definition: concerning a state, one bit of America.
explanation.definitionFit: Statal is a rare adjective meaning relating to a state, such as one of the United States.

clue.text: Father with endless running around got very angry

indicators.note: the letters run about into a new order
the word with loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Dad endlessly running about ended up losing his temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing a fit is an idiom for flying into a rage.

clue.text: Member of family one thanks for providing cold refreshment

parts.note: Gran, a grandmother, is a family member
I is the Roman numeral one
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: A relative is thanked for bringing iced drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A granita is a coarse Italian water ice, a chilled refreshment.

clue.text: Famous economist — the first man's story to be listened to

indicators.note: the phrase is heard rather than read, giving a similar-sounding name

parts.note: Adam was the first man in Genesis, and his story would be a myth

explanation.surface: A noted economist's tale of the original man, told aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam Smith, author of The Wealth of Nations, is the founding figure of classical economics.

clue.text: Rose serves supper initially with grace?

indicators.note: only the opening letter of supper is used

parts.note: grace is a short prayer said before a meal

explanation.surface: Someone named Rose serves supper after first saying grace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like a woman's name or the past of rise; here it is the perforated nozzle of a watering can.
explanation.definitionFit: The rose of a watering can is its spray head, so it is a kind of sprinkling device.

clue.text: Imagine having drink with model

parts.note: to sup is to drink
a model poses for an artist

explanation.surface: Picture yourself having a drink with a fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: To suppose something is to assume or imagine it to be the case.

clue.text: Endless cereal, to an excessive degree? Then get a cheese

indicators.note: the grain word drops its last letter

parts.note: rice is a cereal crop
OTT, over the top, means excessive

explanation.surface: After an endless excess of cereal, someone finally gets some cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricotta is a soft Italian whey cheese.

clue.text: Get irritable about journey in ship

indicators.note: the bad-tempered word goes around the next piece

parts.note: arsy is British slang for bad-tempered or irritable
a go can be a trip or journey

explanation.surface: Someone turns grumpy about a voyage on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: ARSY is British slang for touchy or bad-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: An argosy is a large merchant ship, especially of Renaissance Ragusa or Venice.

clue.text: Spy in railway compartment

definitions.meaning: an agent planted long in advance, waiting to be activated
a berth or carriage with beds on an overnight train

explanation.surface: An undercover agent on board a night train.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeper is both a dormant agent and a train compartment with beds.

clue.text: Discharge starts to pollute everywhere in holiday region

indicators.note: the opening letters go inside the holiday region

parts.note: the South-West of England, SW, is a popular British holiday area

indicators.note: only the opening letters of the two following words are used

explanation.surface: Discharges are beginning to pollute everything in a tourist area.
explanation.walkthrough: SW is the South-West of England, the holiday counties of Devon and Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: To spew is to pour out or discharge in a flood.

clue.text: Quiet maestro accompanying dog and horse?

parts.note: P is piano, the musical marking for quiet
an ace is an expert, a master
a setter is a breed of gun dog

explanation.surface: A soft-spoken conductor walking his dog and his horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: a horse can make the pace in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: In a race a horse may be the leader setting the speed for the field, so it is one example.

clue.text: See 6 down
Sound of extraordinary triumph I quietly released

indicators.note: out of the ordinary, so the remaining letters are put in a new order
the next two pieces are let go from the word triumph

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: A tremendous victory that someone quietly let slip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'released' takes I and P out of TRIUMPH, leaving TRUMH, which 'extraordinary' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrum is a steady drumming or strumming noise.

clue.text: Prisoner touched, it's said, in dispute

parts.note: a con is a convict

indicators.note: the word is to be heard, not read

parts.note: flicked means touched lightly

explanation.surface: An inmate, reportedly a bit mad, is in a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touched' looks like slang for crazy; here it means lightly struck, flicked.
explanation.definitionFit: A conflict is a serious disagreement or clash.

clue.text: Burst in as one bishop getting put out

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a bishop is styled Right Reverend, RR

indicators.note: the word put is knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: A single bishop is annoyed, and storms in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' reads as annoyed, but 'out' only rearranges PUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrupt is to enter forcibly and suddenly, as invaders do.

clue.text: Go away to dine, tucking into small portion

indicators.note: the eating word goes inside the small piece, and tucking into is also a food idiom

parts.note: a bit is a small portion
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: Someone is told to clear off and eat their little serving.
explanation.definitionFit: Beat it is slang for leave at once, an order to clear off.

clue.text: Crooner and lousy actor given support in Spanish building

parts.note: Al Jolson and Al Bowlly were famous crooners
a ham is a bad, over-the-top actor
a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A singer and a poor actor get help at a building in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alhambra is the Moorish palace and fortress complex at Granada.
